title: 10 May 2023
des: DOH (HAAD) paediatrics recall, 10 May 2023 (two recalls with reviewer corrections)

questions.question: A girl has proximal muscle weakness, arthralgia, heliotrope and facial rash, and a positive Gowers sign. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Heliotrope rash with proximal weakness = JDM. Duchenne affects boys and has no rash.

questions.question: A boy has a picture of Kawasaki disease. What is the treatment?
questions.exp: IVIG 2 g/kg plus aspirin.

questions.question: A 4-year-old boy has a painful limp and cannot stand after a URTI; he is systemically well. What do you do?
questions.exp: Likely transient synovitis, but a child who cannot stand needs careful assessment (bloods, ultrasound) to exclude septic arthritis before discharge. The reviewers marked 'no clinical correlation/offer discussion'.
questions.b: Analgesia and send him home without review
questions.d: Offer analgesia, but assess clinically and discuss before sending home

questions.question: A 3-week-old breastfed baby is jaundiced. What do you do next?
questions.exp: Prolonged jaundice (>14 days term) needs split bilirubin to exclude cholestasis.
questions.a: Reassure if well and send home

questions.question: A child has painful vesicles on the face that ulcerate and crust. What is the cause?
questions.exp: Grouped painful vesicles that ulcerate and crust are HSV.

questions.question: A baby has bilateral dilated renal pelves and ureters with a thick bladder wall. What is the diagnosis and test?
questions.exp: PUV is confirmed by MCUG.

questions.question: A child with sickle cell disease has abdominal pain, tachycardia and pallor after a URTI. What type of crisis is it?
questions.exp: The reviewers corrected the key to aplastic crisis (parvovirus after a viral illness). An enlarging spleen with shock would suggest sequestration.

questions.question: An obese girl with a Cushingoid look, irregular periods, high triglycerides and low HDL. What is the advice?
questions.exp: Lifestyle: daily physical activity and healthy diet.

questions.question: A child has fever, sore throat and exudative tonsils; rapid strep test is negative and culture is awaited. What is given?
questions.exp: Penicillin V if treating GAS.

questions.question: A DOH antibiotic policy includes all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Stewardship favours narrow-spectrum agents.

questions.question: A girl has recurrent chest infections, nail candidiasis and recurrent boils that are hard to treat. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: The recall keyed CGD. Recurrent boils with chest infections and candidiasis also fit hyper-IgE (Job) syndrome; check the stem for eczema and high IgE.

questions.question: A 15-year-old with high fever, rash and hepatosplenomegaly is being followed by rheumatology and is now very unwell. What is the complication?
questions.exp: MAS: falling ESR and platelets, high ferritin and triglycerides, liver dysfunction.
questions.b: Systemic JIA with macrophage activation syndrome (secondary HLH)

questions.question: Which score helps decide on antibiotics in streptococcal pharyngitis?
questions.exp: Centor: tonsillar exudate, tender anterior nodes, fever, absence of cough (McIsaac adds age).

questions.question: A child with fever for 8 days and lymphadenopathy is given amoxicillin and develops a rash. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: EBV.

questions.question: What is the most common cause of short stature?
questions.exp: Normal variants are commonest; the reviewers changed the key to familial.

questions.question: A baby has late-onset neonatal sepsis. The mother had chickenpox 2 days before delivery and is a known TB case on treatment. What is the management?
questions.exp: Treat empirically for bacterial and HSV/VZV infection pending results; evaluate the baby for TB separately.
questions.c: Antibiotics and aciclovir until PCR results

questions.question: A child has syncope during exercise and has been taking erythromycin. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Macrolide-induced QT prolongation.

questions.question: A child with a picture of Crohn's colitis (cobblestone mucosa on colonoscopy). What is the first-line treatment?
questions.exp: EEN for induction in paediatric Crohn's; infliximab for severe or fistulising disease.

questions.question: A child has worsening vomiting over weeks, especially in the morning. What do you do?
questions.exp: Morning vomiting suggests raised ICP.

questions.question: A child is hyperactive. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: ADHD.

questions.question: An overweight girl with falling school performance is sleepy all the time. Which test is LEAST needed?
questions.exp: Sleep apnoea and hypothyroidism explain sleepiness; EEG is least useful.

questions.question: A child has an enlarging axillary node over weeks, weight loss, poor appetite and a large mediastinum. What do you do?
questions.exp: Excision biopsy.

questions.question: Which vaccine is contraindicated in HIV infection?
questions.exp: BCG (live) can cause disseminated disease.

questions.question: A 6-year-old has anaphylaxis (picture shown). What do you give?
questions.exp: Under 6: 150 micrograms; 6–12 years: 300 micrograms.

questions.question: All are causes of red cell aplasia EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Iron deficiency reduces haemoglobinisation, not red cell production in the same way; the others are pure red cell aplasias.

questions.question: A child had a seizure and was given lorazepam by paramedics; glucose is 2.1 mmol/L. What next?
questions.exp: Treat hypoglycaemia.

questions.question: A 14-year-old girl has massive menstrual bleeding. What is the next step?
questions.exp: Assess anaemia and haemodynamic stability first.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT raise suspicion of child abuse?
questions.exp: Shins, knees and chin are common accidental sites in mobile toddlers.
questions.a: A 5-year-old with bruises on the buttocks
questions.d: A 3-year-old with bruises over the tibia and chin

questions.question: Which lesion is present at birth?
questions.exp: Port-wine stains are present at birth.

questions.question: A 3-year-old has ocular movements described as nystagmus without other signs. What is the most likely cause?
questions.exp: The reviewers marked idiopathic. Chaotic multidirectional eye movements with myoclonus would instead suggest opsoclonus–myoclonus (neuroblastoma).

questions.question: Diazoxide in neonatal hyperinsulinism: all of the following are true EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Diazoxide causes sodium and fluid retention (given with chlorothiazide), not diuresis.
questions.c: It opens K-ATP channels (increases potassium permeability)

questions.question: About acute bronchiolitis, all are true EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Post-bronchiolitic wheeze is common in all children, not just atopic ones.
questions.c: It causes persistent wheeze only in allergic patients
questions.d: It is most severe at 2–6 months

questions.question: What is the main cause of fat malabsorption in a child from a developing country with chronic diarrhoea?
questions.exp: Giardia causes steatorrhoea, bloating and weight loss; treat with metronidazole.

questions.question: A baby has late-onset sepsis; the mother has TB. What do you give?
questions.exp: Treat the sepsis; assess TB exposure separately.
questions.b: Antibiotics and treatment for latent TB

questions.question: What does a p-value below 0.05 mean?
questions.exp: p<0.05 is conventionally statistically significant.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT basic research?
questions.exp: Studies in children are clinical research.
questions.c: Drug pharmacodynamics in an animal model

questions.question: What is similar between seasonal and perennial allergic rhinitis?
questions.exp: Intranasal steroids are the most effective treatment for both.
questions.b: Both are caused by pollen only

questions.question: Which test compares two normally distributed values?
questions.exp: t-test.

questions.question: A neonate a few hours old is greyish, cyanosed, with thready pulse and a forceful apex. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: HLHS.

questions.question: What is the incidence of anorexia nervosa in adolescent girls?
questions.exp: About 0.5%.

questions.question: Bilateral renal pelvis dilatation in a neonate. What is the key investigation?
questions.exp: MCUG to exclude PUV/VUR.

questions.question: In which situation is it inappropriate to withdraw life-sustaining treatment?
questions.exp: A child's refusal alone does not justify withdrawing life-sustaining treatment.

questions.question: A 2-year-old with Patau syndrome has intestinal obstruction; the parents want the best treatment. What is the next action?
questions.exp: If the child has survived beyond infancy and parents want treatment, surgery to relieve obstruction is reasonable.

questions.question: What is NOT true about contraindications to breastfeeding?
questions.exp: PKU babies can partially breastfeed.
questions.b: HIV is a contraindication in developed countries

questions.question: A child with SCD is recently pale. What is the likely crisis?
questions.exp: Parvovirus.

questions.question: An obese girl has hirsutism and irregular cycles. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: PCOS.

questions.question: An 8-year-old has hyperthyroidism with a small firm goitre and T4 50. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Graves (TRAb positive).

questions.question: A 10-year-old has irregular sleep and poor school performance after a febrile illness; he was previously good and has not gone out for a week. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: The recall keyed PANDAS (post-streptococcal). Check the stem for OCD symptoms or tics.

questions.question: A 4-year-old has hip pain on internal rotation after a viral infection. What do you do?
questions.exp: Transient synovitis.

questions.question: A 10-year-old athlete has had a stiff knee for 6 months, now inflamed; aspirate is turbid with neutrophils and lymphocytes. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Chronic monoarthritis over 6 weeks = oligoarticular JIA; inflammatory fluid.

questions.question: A 10-year-old with a limp has widening of the joint line on X-ray (slipped femoral epiphysis). What is the treatment?
questions.exp: SCFE: in-situ pinning; Perthes: osteotomy in older children.

questions.question: A child has syncope during sport. What is the most likely cause?
questions.exp: Exertional syncope is cardiac until proven otherwise.

questions.question: An adolescent boy injured his knuckles punching a wall. What do you do?
questions.exp: Use HEADSSS in private; consider anger, mood, abuse. The reviewers keyed 'offer privacy and discussion'.
questions.a: Tell him cartilage may be destroyed
questions.b: Treat the injury and offer privacy and discussion about what happened

questions.question: A 14-year-old girl took 8 paracetamol tablets yesterday and 10 today to harm herself. What do you do?
questions.exp: Staggered overdose: start NAC immediately with level and LFTs; psychiatric assessment once medically fit.
questions.a: Start NAC and admit to a mental health unit with 1:1 nursing
questions.c: Obtain the level then decide; give charcoal
questions.d: Obtain a level and start NAC

questions.question: A child has haematuria and an abdominal mass. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Wilms.

questions.question: Opsoclonus–myoclonus in neuroblastoma responds to which treatment?
questions.exp: OMAS is paraneoplastic and autoimmune; neurological symptoms need immunotherapy even after tumour removal.

questions.question: A 10-year-old with Down syndrome has decreasing activity, haemoptysis, cyanosis and hepatosplenomegaly. What is the next step?
questions.exp: Eisenmenger syndrome: inoperable; discuss prognosis and supportive care.
questions.b: Explain the situation and prognosis to the parents

questions.question: What distinguishes Patau from Edwards syndrome?
questions.exp: Cleft lip/palate is typical of Patau.

questions.question: A 13-year-old prepubertal girl has BP 140/90, fatigue and swollen hands. Which test will diagnose the cause of hypertension?
questions.exp: Turner syndrome (lymphoedema, delayed puberty) with coarctation causing hypertension.

questions.question: A neonate has clitoromegaly, 46,XX karyotype, normal blood count and electrolytes. What is the next test?
questions.exp: CAH work-up.

questions.question: A child has metabolic acidosis, hypokalaemia, hyperchloraemia and glycosuria. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Proximal tubulopathy.

questions.question: A fair-skinned child with learning disability has a musty odour. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: PKU.

questions.question: Which condition is NOT included in the neonatal screening programme (as recalled)?
questions.exp: UK screening includes PKU, IVA, MSUD and homocystinuria; galactosaemia is not screened. (The recall keyed homocystinuria, which IS screened in the UK since 2015.)

questions.question: Which amino acids are restricted in maple syrup urine disease?
questions.exp: Branched-chain amino acids.

questions.question: What is the triple test for Down syndrome in pregnancy?
questions.exp: Triple test.

questions.question: A 25-week neonate ventilated on day 4 has platelets of 50 ×10⁹/L and dropping. What is the cause?
questions.exp: Late thrombocytopenia suggests sepsis/NEC.

questions.question: A 2-year-old playing with toys becomes sick with tachycardia, enlarged liver, bilateral crackles (more on the right) and thready pulse. What is the cause?
questions.exp: Hepatomegaly and bilateral crackles = heart failure.

questions.question: A neonate with SVT reversed by adenosine has multiple small atrial tumours on echo and a brain mass at the foramen of Monro. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Rhabdomyomas and SEGA.

questions.question: Which is NOT a risk factor for neonatal hypocalcaemia?
questions.exp: Maternal HYPERparathyroidism suppresses the fetal parathyroids and causes neonatal hypocalcaemia; maternal hypoparathyroidism causes fetal hyperparathyroidism.

questions.question: Which statement about bronchiolitis is NOT correct?
questions.exp: Post-bronchiolitic wheeze is common regardless of atopy.
questions.c: It causes persistent wheezes only in allergic children

questions.question: What is the treatment for persistent asthma?
questions.exp: Low-dose ICS is the preventer.

questions.question: A 5-week-old is jaundiced. What do you check first?
questions.exp: The reviewers wrote total + indirect, but the purpose is to measure conjugated bilirubin.

questions.question: A 3-week-old jaundiced baby has ALT 90 and pale stools for 2 days. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Pale stools = biliary atresia until proven otherwise.

questions.question: A 5-year-old girl has two café-au-lait macules (1.5 cm and 0.5 cm). What is true?
questions.exp: Two macules do not meet NF1 criteria; review for new features.
questions.c: Size does not reflect severity; follow up for other features
questions.d: Absence of axillary freckling makes NF1 unlikely

questions.question: Which is NOT a reason to start antiepileptic drugs after a first seizure?
questions.exp: Prolactin helps distinguish seizures from non-epileptic events but is not an indication for treatment.

questions.question: Which is inherited as autosomal dominant?
questions.exp: EB simplex.

questions.question: A child has nasal polyps. What is the most likely underlying diagnosis?
questions.exp: Nasal polyps in a child need a sweat test.

questions.question: What is the level of injury in Erb palsy?
questions.exp: Upper trunk.
